newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-VERMEIL ENDING 15-YEAR ABSENCE TO COACH RAMS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-VERMEIL ENDING 15-YEAR ABSENCE TO COACH RAMS.

text.p: Dick Vermeil, who walked away from NFL coaching 15 years ago complaining of 'burnout', rejoined the ranks Tuesday by signing on as head coach of the St Louis Rams.
The 61-year-old Vermeil, who took the Philadelphia Eagles to the Super Bowl after the 1980 season, replaces Rich Brooks, who was fired following a 6-10 season.

The 15-year gap between head coaching jobs is the longest in NFL history. The next closest was Ted Marchibroda, who was coach of the Baltimore Colts and went 13 years before being hired again by the Indianapolis Colts in 1992.
Vermeil, who turned to television commentating after leaving the sidelines, coached the Eagles to their only Super Bowl appearance, a 27-10 loss to the Oakland Raiders in Super Bowl XV.
He guided Philadelphia to an overall record of 57-51, including playoffs, and took his teams to the postseason every year from 1978 to 1981 and won two NFC East titles.
He resigned in 1982 after seven seasons, becoming the first coach to cite burnout as the reason for leaving.
Before coming to the Eagles, Vermeil coached two seasons at UCLA and took the Bruins to the Rose Bowl following the 1975 campaign.
Vermeil was not the first choice of the Rams.

Team president John Shaw made repeated attempts to hire George Seifert after Seifert stepped down as head coach of the San Francisco 49ers last week. Shaw also was interested in Jacksonville Jaguars offensive coordinator Kevin Gilbride, who was named head coach of the San Diego Chargers.
"This is my last stop. It's an unbelievable opportunity," an excited Vermeil said at a news conference Tuesday.

"People will say Vermeil is a retread, he's 60 years old, he's over the hill," he said. "I have a passion for coaching and a passion for the people I coach. The game of football has not changed all that much."
Vermeil said concerns of the past are not a worry now. "I have overloaded because I get too emotional and too intense," he conceded. "In 14 years, I've learned how to handle it."
His work as an NFL analyst for CBS and on college football telecasts the last nine years for ABC has kept him prepared.
"I have received a PHD from the greatest graduate school in pro football," said Vermeil.
